title: Bira Circuit
description:
What people are saying By David F โ€ Pattaya's racing circuit โ€ 4.0 of 5 bubbles Sep 2018 Great circuit and next door is a fantastic go kart track. Really nice row of shady trees to sit under and a good grand stand. By Roger โ€ Exciting weekend for car and go-kart racing โ€ 4.0 of 5 bubbles Sep 2018 If you're resident in Pattaya, or even Bangkok, and also a motor racing fan, then a visit to the Bira Circuit is recommended to get the pulse racing. 
The venue is a 30-minute drive south-east of Central Patttaya, on Highway 36, and boasts 2 circuits, one for cars and bikes, and another for go-kart racing.
2.4 kilometres in length, it's more suitable for bikes and economy / family-sized tin-tops, but perhaps a little short for larger capacity and faster racing cars.
On my first visit, the modest THB 100 daily entrance fee provided 6 races for each of the 2 days (Saturday & Sunday), beginning 10 am. until 5.30 pm. 10 of the races were for tin-tops, and the remaining 2 for fearsome, full-race Chevrolet Camaros. Practice days were on the previous Thursday and Friday.  Attendance appeared quite low and very easily accommodated by the one and only grandstand. 
On the positive side, lunch time and the end of the day allows entrance to the pit area where you can photograph the cars, drivers, crew and pretty sales promotion girls in a relaxed and friendly atmosphere.
It's possible to walk around half of the circuit, and I would recommend the first corner after the grid & main straight, where there's a tricky bend with adverse camber which doubles back to the next bend, a hairpin, where you can also spectate from.
On the negative side, facilities are fairly rudimentary, especially food services.
Unless you sit in the covered grandstand all day, take an umbrella (for shade or rain), a mat and a folding chair to watch the action in relative comfort. What is Travelersโ€ Choice? title: 2Sky Pattaya-Rocket Ball
description: "2 SKY PATTAYA Rocket-Ball is a truly breathtaking experience where two brave riders are catapulted high up into the air at totally thrilling speeds, spinning and bouncing as they go!!! " What is it Rocket Ball?The Rocket Ball ride, consists of two steel towers with a special cord connected to each tower. The other ends of the cords are attached to a caged steel vehicle in which 2 riders are seated. The vehicle is pulled to the ground, where riders board. When the vehicle is released from the loading station, the cords engage, sending riders on a high-speed vertical launch 50 meters into midair at speeds of 100 KPH in one second and 5G force power. Rocket Ball to the sky! To call the Rocket Ball the most thrilling, exciting, amazing experience is no understatement. Two towers and one gondole allows to be catapulted into the air, going from 0 to 100 KPH in one second. No doubt about it, itโ€s the ultimate rush.Who operates behind the scenes of 2Sky Pattaya - Rocket Ball?Our team here at 2Sky Pattaya, are trained and qualified to the fullest extent by Technical Park. 2Sky Pattaya is also fully supervised by an on-site European technical engineer/master.Is it safe?of course it is! the passengers are first secured by a four point harness (such as what you would find in a rally car for example) A padded safety bar is then locked into position in front of the passengers. Each pair of cords has a determined lifespan which is monitored very closely. Each 'jump' is recorded by computer which then generates a regular safety report and tells the operator when the cords are due to be replaced. and if that wasn't enough, in the highly improbable event of a cord failing there is an additional failure safety system bound into the elastics of the cord to prevent the gondola falling. We also have a highly skilled team of engineers here at 2Sky Pattaya who carry out daily checks and maintenance but Technical Park-Italy also carry out an annual safety inspection before the attraction is deemed safe for operation. These safety reports are available upon request to members of the public. What is Travelersโ€ Choice? By David B โ€ Why Keep it Secret? โ€ 4.0 of 5 bubbles May 2016 Wat Yai Inthraram  is one of the most important Buddhist temples in Chonburi.  It dates back to the early Ayutthaya period (14th century).  The base of the temple is built in the curved shape of a junk ship

The main attraction of Wat Yai Inthraram is the murals on the walls of the Ubosoth, but most of the time the doors are closed and entrance is forbidden.  

Fortunately we struck on a day when a monk was opening the doors and he allowed us in, but forbade us to take photographs, so we have none to share with you on this review.  (Perhaps like the paintings in the tombs in  the Valley of the Kings in Egypt, they are frightened that flashlight will deteriorate the paintings).

The murals, some of them dating back hundreds of years, are colourful depictions of the Buddha's 10 previous lives.

Why these treasures are not more publicly available is a mystery. What is Travelersโ€ Choice? What people are saying By Tomas, Sweden โ€ Back, and head massage โ€ 5.0 of 5 bubbles Mar 2020 This was amazing! Professional massage. The place looks small on the outside. The sign are red so it's easy to find on the street. My massage was an hour. I'm so relaxed, and my back feel wonderful. They have a few chairs for feet massage. More of the massage tables. By MrKim โ€ Looking for professional Thai massage in Pattaya? โ€ 5.0 of 5 bubbles Oct 2019 Whilst there are a vast number of Thai Massage Shops throughout Thailand trying to find a good one is sometimes a challenge. In the provinces the massages and mainly for local Thais and they know what they want, unfortunately in many tourist destinations the quality is often compromised by the demand from tourists with non or minimal experience of Thai massage.

Pattaya is a classic tourist destination and there must be at least 4,000 shops around the city, so how to choose. First rule is to get off the main tourist roads and explore some side streets. If the ladies outside are somewhat seductive in their attempts to lure you inside, their intentions may not be to provide with a traditional massage!

Having recently moved to Pattaya I have been looking for a good and reliable massage shop. I avoid the flashy large salons and prefer the smaller places as the massage is generally more professional and relaxing. Through a personal recommendation I was recommended to Massaging Hands located on Soi Buakhao! Now this is not an area that I would normally to expect good massage but I was in for a pleasant surprise.

Massaging Hands is a simply decorated shop with the ladies sitting outside waiting for customers. Despite the simplicity one will note that the place is spotlessly clean and well organised. Massaging Hands has a full License for massage and all the ladies have Diplomas from massage schools. Mai the manager even graduated from Wat Po, the most prestigious Massage School in Thailand.

Massaging Hands offers Traditional Thai Massage, Oil Massage and Foot Massage with further specialist massages including Neck & Shoulder, Hot Stone & Hot Herb.

The massage that I received from Noy was excellent. I like strong massage and I also like that the therapist stretches my arms and legs. Noy was excellent with enough pressure to tease out the knots in my muscles and tendons without causing any pain. I know that she has passed the stringent tests for massage and felt safe in her hands. After 1 hour of manipulation, a neck massage and a head massage I felt rejuvenated and ready to explore Soi Boukhao!

On another occasion I was suffering from a lot of pain in my shoulder and upper arm and Mai recommended an intensive back, neck and shoulder massage. Starting low in my back she found twisted ligaments, tense muscles and other lumps of tissue that needed her full attention and also challenged her knowledge of anatomy. It has taken 3 sessions to resolve the problem and under Maiโ€s expert therapy the pain is now minimal and normal movements are now possible.

A massage shop is rather like a barber/hairdresser, once you find a place that you like you will return. You get to know the staff and the therapists that you prefer. You are also assured that each massage will be of a consistent high quality, so I guess that you will know where I will be returning for my massages in the future! What is Travelersโ€ Choice? title: Flintstones Taxi Service
description:
What people are saying By domyno50 โ€ Good service, great locations โ€ 4.0 of 5 bubbles Dec 2019 We hired Flintstones Taxi (also goes by Left Luggage Service) for a City tour of Pattaya when we were in port on a cruise vacation. There were 5 of us. 

Transportation was a van that was comfortable. 

Our guide was late to pick us up and we had to have a local person call him to make sure of what time and where he was going to meet us.  He was also not prepared for the day as our first stop was to a gas station as his tank was on empty. He purchased water for us at the gas station. 

Driver spoke broken English but enough to share a few pieces of info and get important details across to us/answer basic questions. 

We did our homework in advance and requested sites that we wanted to visit. The tour was not coordinated by this company. 

The driver was very helpful in purchasing tickets for us at our stops (he told us the price from the website of each place, that he showed us, and we gave him money), this reduced any language issues at ticket counters. 

The driver was prompt and on time to pick us up at all locations. 

Despite a shaky start, we had a great day in Pattaya. Be the first to upload a photo Upload a photo

title: Tony's Fitness Gym
description:
What people are saying By Sam C โ€ Super โ€ 5.0 of 5 bubbles Sep 2021 Tony's gym was the best bargain on the planet. When I started coming to Pattaya in 2002, he had several large venues. My favorite was a spa that felt like an airline hanger on third road. You walk in and the ambiance floats you away. You take a shower then they lead you to a eucaliptus sauna, which gets you all steeped up. Then small pools for one, hot as hades, and you jump in and boil like a lobster. While there they serve you a tangerine. It's those nice touches that make you feel special. From there it is back and forth to the ice baths several times. In the end, it is an invigorating and memorable experience. But about two years later they closed it and tour it down! 

Then there is Tony's Gym. The cold pool was my favorite place in the heat of the summer. I could site there for twenty minutes and imerge shaken, not stirred, by the temperature--it reached my core and really cooled me down. They used to have classes in this or that--it was a fun place. But the first manager was a thief and he stole all the lifetime memberhsip cards that were registered with him, and claimed in a straight face that there was some paperwork problem. The office of course never recieved the documents and I had to pay another 20,000 bhat to the company. They were lax but that is what to expect in Pattaya if you don't realize who you are dealing with. Never had a problem after that. Good people. I loved the place. description:
What people are saying By Brad C โ€ Do not use Grab Thailand! โ€ 1.0 of 5 bubbles Mar 2024 Grab drivers are incompetent and downright frightening at times. Most of the Grab drivers are extremely greedy and will ask for extra money for anything possible.  One got lost in a rural area, picked a random spot, said we had arrived "the back way," and expected us just to get out there and give him money. That same one refused to stop to allow passengers to alight, keeping the rear doors and windows locked. A complaint to Grab Thailand was met with disinterest and vague promises to "take action." By Kjell Magne K โ€ Pattaya Taxis are the worst and they are the reason that you should not visit Pattaya at all โ€ 1.0 of 5 bubbles Jan 2020 If possible, NEVER EVER sit in a taxi in Pattaya.

Not any of the taxis in Pattaya will go by taximeter, they just say that it is standard price. Their standard price is almost three times as much as the taximeter would show. Our first night here they wanted 200 Baht for a short trip and we asked many different taxis, we just said "NO WAY" and walked instead. The trip should have been like 70 to 80 Baht in the beginning, but when we had walked closer, it should have been minimum price and they still said 200 Baht, one taxi even asked for 300 Baht.

Today we asked for a trip to Nong Nooch Botanical Garden and that is a trip of about 25 kilometers and should have costed around 250 Baht according to the Taxi's own overview of fares (which we found in the pocket in the back of the front seats). They started with 700 Baht, and went quickly down to 500 Baht, but we got the trip for 400 Baht after some haggling. On the return trip it was not possible to haggle at all so the price was 500 Baht.

The worst thing is that it seems that the hotels are also into this, it might be that they get some percentage if they call for a taxi.
